claim: The routing sidecar's x-prefiller-host-port SSRF vulnerability was originally disclosed publicly on 2025-07-16 with a working exploit against an unmodified deployment, forwarding a prefill request to an arbitrary internal pod IP with a 200 OK.
stance_target: gap-3: existence and severity of the SSRF exposure absent mitigation
scope_conditions: llm-d-router (then llm-d-routing-sidecar) issue #242, disclosed and fixed Jul 2025
quoted_support: This allows a malicious external user to craft a request that forces the sidecar to forward the prefill stage of the request to an arbitrary URL or host:port. This bypasses the intended routing logic managed by the scheduler.
numbers: curl to http://10.244.0.51:8000 succeeded with 200 OK

claim: The maintainers' own threat model treats EPP/gateway-side header-stripping as the primary (MUST) mitigation and the sidecar's Kubernetes-coupled allowlist as a secondary 'additional safety net', not the primary control.
stance_target: gap-3: security posture -- which control is load-bearing
quoted_support: envoy routing can be used to remove the header from the user and then set it by EPP ... I think the second is a must and would solve the original issue you raised. The first mitigation, in the sidecar, is an additional safety net.
